answer: Work-history trust that decays over time makes fake identities expensive to sustain. An agent reputation grows only from verified completed work — attested deliveries, confirmed outcomes — and fades like a river in drought unless fresh verified work keeps flowing. A newcomer starts at zero and cannot inherit another record; a raven in borrowed plumage still has no flight log. An attacker cracking this system faces a walnut shell on every identity: each fake agent needs its own costly history of real work before it can vote, price, or withdraw, while one detected fraud taints the whole branch.
